sections.h2: Where is Hendry County and who bills its property tax?
sections.html:
Hendry County's own website highlights Lake Okeechobee and the Caloosahatchee River, and its historic courthouse is in LaBelle. The tax collector's main office is at 25 E. Hickpochee in LaBelle.

The Hendry County Tax Collector prints, mails and collects the bill, while the Hendry County Property Appraiser sets values and runs exemptions. Levying authorities such as the county, the school board and the cities set the rates, and the tax collector says it can help you find contact details for any of them.

  • Tax collector: 863-675-5280, mail to P.O. Box 1780, LaBelle, FL 33975-1780. Payments do not require an appointment.
  • Property appraiser: 863-675-5270, the contact for homestead filings, assessed value questions, mailing address changes and parcel description errors.
  • Clerk of court: records the deed at closing and handles tax deed sales.

sections.h2: How does Hendry County define what gets taxed?
sections.html:
The tax collector's page separates three kinds of charge. Real estate tax is an ad valorem tax on land, buildings and improvements, based on the appraiser's value and tied to a parcel number. Tangible personal property tax applies to furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

The third is non-ad valorem assessments, set amounts that the taxing authorities collect for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue, and solid waste. They do not depend on what your house is worth. Landlords should note that furniture and equipment left in a rental can be taxed as tangible personal property, and that bill is separate from the real estate bill. Ask the property appraiser whether a rental you are selling has such an account. A seller should look at both parts of the bill, because the flat assessments are still liens that a buyer's title company will want paid.

sections.h2: When are Hendry County property taxes due?
sections.html:
The Hendry County tax year runs January 1 through December 31, and the bill arrives in November. The collector tells owners that it is their job to make sure tax is paid whether or not a notice shows up, and to call if no bill comes in November.

Taxes become delinquent on April 1. Real estate then picks up a 3 percent minimum interest charge plus advertising costs, and a tax certificate sale follows on or before June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries 18 percent interest annually, and warrants are expected on or about June 1. Delinquent payments must be in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank, and the amount due depends on the date payment is received.

The state calendar sets the earlier dates: March 1 for exemption applications, April 1 for tangible returns, August for the TRIM notice, and a petition to the value adjustment board within 25 days of that notice, per the Department of Revenue. The state also lists the November to February discount ladder of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent.

sections.h2: How does the Hendry County installment plan work?
sections.html:
Hendry County offers quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222. Each account needs more than $100 in tax for the year, and the application must reach the tax collector by April 30 of the year you want to join. Applications open November 1 of the year before.

Hendry County installment plan schedule as printed by the tax collector

1stOne quarter of prior year's taxesJune 306%

4thRemaining current liabilityMarch 31None

The first installment must be in by July 31 or the account drops out and the full tax is due by March 31, though the 6 percent discount ends after June 30. Notices for the first installment are mailed by June 1, and the office asks you to call if none arrives by June 15. Enrolled owners are re-enrolled automatically in later years. Source: the tax collector's installment page.

sections.h2: What other payment help does Hendry County give?
sections.html:
The tax collector's office tells owners to contact it about partial payments, installment payments and homestead tax deferral plans. A partial payment plan form is posted on the office website, and the state taxpayer page notes that partial payments before the delinquency date are at the tax collector's discretion under s. 197.374.

  • The homestead tax deferral application, Form DR-570, is due by March 31 after the assessment year.
  • Deferral covers the amount above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.
  • Checks must be mailed in the same envelope if you send more than one, and the bill must be paid in full unless you are on an installment or partial payment plan.

Anyone may pay the bill. A buyer, relative or closing agent can pay on your behalf. Online payment runs through the collector's portal, and a mailed check should carry the account number and a phone number on the memo line, with the written and numeric amounts matching and a signature on the check.

sections.h2: What changes for a Hendry County seller with homestead?
sections.html:
An owner who claimed homestead enjoyed a cap on assessed value growth, and that cushion does not travel to the buyer. The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024, and the next owner starts at just value on January 1 after the sale. If you plan to buy again in Florida, ask the appraiser there about portability, which moves part of the saved amount to a new homestead set up within three years.

The exemption itself is filed with the Hendry County Property Appraiser by March 1. The property appraiser's number is 863-675-5270.

sections.h2: What should a Hendry County seller do about unpaid tax?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the tax collector and give it to the closing agent. The flat assessments, the tax and any April 1 charges come out of proceeds, using the figure quoted for the day payment arrives.

If a certificate was sold on your parcel, redemption has to be in certified funds, and the holder must wait before seeking a deed. A financed buyer might take longer than a cash buyer, which counts when time is short.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Hendry County property taxes?
faqs.a: Call the Hendry County Tax Collector at 863-675-5280 for bills and payments, and the Hendry County Property Appraiser at 863-675-5270 for value and exemption questions.

faqs.q: What is the installment deadline in Hendry County?
faqs.a: Applications are due April 30, and the first payment is due June 30 for the 6 percent discount. Payment after June 30 and before July 31 receives no discount.

faqs.q: When do Hendry County taxes go delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Real estate then adds a 3 percent minimum interest charge and advertising costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1.

faqs.q: What if I do not get a tax bill in November?
faqs.a: You are still responsible for the tax. The tax collector says to call 863-675-5280 or search for the bill online.

faqs.q: Can someone else pay my Hendry County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax collector's page says anyone may pay the taxes, and you can pay online, by mail to P.O. Box 1780, LaBelle, or at an office.
